stem: During vaccine preparation, which action should be avoided?

options.text: Select the lateral thigh in an infant under 12 months
Use the deltoid in a child older than 12 months
Consider whether the child has special vaccine requirements
Refer complex immunisation needs to a specialist immunisation clinic

explanation: Prime the administration needle should be avoided during vaccine preparation. The other options describe appropriate site selection or appropriate assessment and referral for children with special immunisation needs.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: National Immunisation Schedule and Immunisation for Special Populations

optionExplanations.A: Correct because priming the administration needle is specifically listed as an action not to do.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because the lateral thigh is the recommended injection site in infants under 12 months.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because the deltoid is an appropriate site in children older than 12 months.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because assessing for special vaccine requirements is appropriate practice.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because referral to a specialist immunisation clinic is appropriate for complex immunisation needs.

sourceRefs: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
